card.name: The Cosmic Alphabet Soup
card.power: Entropy Drain. Tap this card to force your opponent to randomly shuffle their deck until absolute disorder is achieved.
card.lore: The universe leans toward chaos. But given infinite time, randomness accidentally spells out perfect, brief order.

line: The Cosmic Alphabet Soup, Entropy Drain? The universe leans toward chaos, but randomness accidentally spells out perfect, brief order.

card.name: The Floating Space-Brain
card.power: Existential Crisis. Target player must skip their next turn while questioning if their entire hand was randomly generated an artificial second ago.
card.lore: You never evolved. You are just a random statistical blip of order with fake memories of a past that never happened.

line: The Floating Space-Brain, Existential Crisis: you never evolved; a statistical blip with fake memories of a past that never happened.

card.name: Entropy's Final Prank
card.power: Cosmic Joke. Instantly cancels any Purpose or Meaning cards on the table.
card.lore: Scientific models predicting infinite universes also predict you are a fake space-brain. If the math leads to absurd pranks, the math is broken.

line: Entropy's Final Prank, Cosmic Joke: cancels any Purpose or Meaning. If the math leads to absurd pranks, the math is broken.

card.name: The Fake Memory Implant
card.power: Gaslight. Rewrite one rule of the game. If the opponent notices, claim it has been that way since their birth.
card.lore: You trust your senses, but every memory of your childhood is just data injected into your random, transient consciousness.

line: The Fake Memory Implant, Gaslight: rewrite one rule. Opponent notices? Claim it has been that way since birth.

card.name: The Room of the Mind
card.power: Solitary Confinement. Exile all other players' Entity cards. They were never real anyway.
card.lore: You are the only audience member in a very convincing dream. Nothing outside your skull can be proven to exist.

line: The Room of the Mind, Solitary Confinement: the only audience member in a very convincing dream. They were never real anyway.

card.name: Descartes' Doubt-Demon
card.power: Erase Reality. Destroy all Field cards. Only Thought cards remain in play.
card.lore: Doubt everything—your senses, your body, the sky. The only absolute certainty is that you are thinking. I think, therefore I am trapped.

line: Descartes' Doubt-Demon, Erase Reality: doubt everything, your senses, your body, the sky. I think, therefore I am trapped.

card.name: The Void Projection
card.power: Auto-Generate Script. Play your opponent's cards for them, since they are merely figments of your imagination.
card.lore: Your barista, your best friend, your dog—all just high-definition holograms rendered by your lonely, desperate mind.

line: The Void Projection, Auto-Generate Script: barista, best friend, dog, all holograms rendered by your lonely, desperate mind.

card.name: The Empathy Choice
card.power: Leap of Faith. Give an opponent 5 health points just to pretend the multiplayer mode isn't a solo campaign.
card.lore: Believing other people exist requires blind faith. We choose to act like others are real because the alternative is unbearable isolation.

line: The Empathy Choice, Leap of Faith: pretend the multiplayer mode isn't a solo campaign. The alternative is unbearable isolation.

card.name: The Vaporizer Beam
card.power: High-Tech Suicide. Destroy your own strongest card to instantly spawn an identical token on the other side of the board.
card.lore: It's not a fast travel machine. It's a murder booth that scans your data right before incinerating your original body.

line: The Vaporizer Beam, High-Tech Suicide? Not a fast travel machine. A murder booth.

card.name: The Perfect Copy
card.power: Identity Theft. Inherits all stats, buffs, and memories of the vaporized original. Feels exactly like the original. Is not the original.
card.lore: Built from scratch from new atoms in a new place. It laughs like you, it remembers being you, but YOU died at the airport.

line: The Perfect Copy, Identity Theft: it laughs like you, remembers being you, but YOU died at the airport.

card.name: Parfit's Shipyard
card.power: Psychological Continuity. Whenever a card is destroyed, its spirit token moves to a new machine without penalty.
card.lore: Personal identity doesn't matter. What matters is the continuity of your psychological patterns. You are just software.

line: Parfit's Shipyard, Psychological Continuity: personal identity doesn't matter. You are just software.

card.name: The Prestige Glitch
card.power: Double Trouble. If the Vaporizer Beam fails, duplicate the card. Both believe they are the real player. Both must fight to the death.
card.lore: What if the machine forgets to kill the original? You are now two people sharing a past, forced into a psychological horror story.

line: The Prestige Glitch machine forgets to kill the original? Both must fight to the death.

card.name: The Unliftable Rock
card.power: Logical Booby-Trap. Play this to permanently stall any All-Powerful boss card.
card.lore: Can an all-powerful being create a rock so heavy they cannot lift it? If yes, they lack power. If no, they lack power. Gotcha.

line: The Unliftable Rock booby-trap: if yes, they lack power. If no, they lack power. Gotcha.

card.name: The Semantic Trap
card.power: Failure of Language. Counter any spell by proving the spell's wording is technically nonsensical jibberish.
card.lore: ESVIOND. COFFEIRE Asking someone to do the logically impossible isn't a test of power; it's just mashing contradictory words together like an idiot.

line: The Semantic Trap, Failure of Language: technically nonsensical jibberish, mashing contradictory words together like an idiot.

card.name: The Delegating Boss-Hog
card.power: Surrender Control. Give away your best cards to your opponent. Your passive income multiplier increases by 10x.
card.lore: True power isn't doing everything yourself. An absolute control-freak burns out. Giving up control actually makes your power stronger.

line: The Delegating Boss-Hog, Surrender Control: give away your best cards. An absolute control-freak burns out.

card.name: C.S. Lewis' Red Pen
card.power: Veto Nonsense. Cancel a play because the premise is flawed.
card.lore: Meaningless combinations of words do not suddenly acquire meaning simply because we prefix them with the words "God can".

line: C.S. Lewis' Red Pen, Veto Nonsense: the premise is flawed. Meaningless combinations of words do not suddenly acquire meaning.

card.name: The Door of Existence
card.power: Forced Entry. Spawn a new card onto the field. It instantly takes 5 existential damage because nobody asked it to be here.
card.lore: Behind the door is a slice of cake and a pit of snakes. Creating life is pushing someone through without telling them what's behind it.

opener: Here is something nobody asked for
line: The Door of Existence. Forced Entry. Behind the door, a slice of cake and a pit of snakes.

card.name: The Snake Pit of Life
card.power: Inevitable Struggle. All newly played cards are immediately burdened with a Lifelong Maintenance tax token.
card.lore: No matter how good life gets, it guarantees pain, loss, and struggle. It is a risk the unborn never agreed to take.

line: The Snake Pit of Life, Inevitable Struggle: pain, loss, and struggle, a risk the unborn never agreed to take.

card.name: Benatar's Asymmetry
card.power: Better Never To Have Been. Banish a card to the void. It feels no pain, and since it doesn't exist, it doesn't miss out on pleasure.
card.lore: The absence of pain is good. The absence of pleasure is not bad if there is no one to miss it. Non-existence wins the math.

line: Benatar's Asymmetry, Better Never To Have Been: banish a card to the void. Non-existence wins the math.

card.name: The Litigious Offspring
card.power: Sue Your Maker. Deal damage directly to the player who spawned you for the crime of bringing you into the game without consent.
card.lore: You don't owe them for the gift of life. There was no you to receive the gift before they forced you into the rollercoaster.

line: The Litigious Offspring, Sue Your Maker: the crime of bringing you into the game without consent. You don't owe them.

card.name: The Autopilot Brain
card.power: Invisible Strings. Take control of an opponent's card. Explain to them that it was actually their environment that made them do it.
card.lore: You think you're calling the shots. You're just reacting to habits, childhood trauma, and the time of day.

line: The Autopilot Brain, Invisible Strings: you think you're calling the shots; just reacting to habits, childhood trauma, the time of day.

card.name: Libet's Delay
card.power: Pre-Cognitive Strike. Play your turn before you even realize you've made a decision. Skip the conscious awareness phase.
card.lore: The brain gets ready to act, and only afterward do you become conscious of it. You don't make choices; you just watch them happen.

line: Libet's Delay, Pre-Cognitive Strike: skip the conscious awareness phase. You don't make choices; you just watch them happen.

card.name: The Algorithm Feeder
card.power: Engineered Addiction. Force opponent to repeatedly draw cards until their deck runs out, convincing them they chose to keep scrolling.
card.lore: Your phone knows your bedtime better than your mom. You didn't freely choose to click; the algorithm studied you like a lab rat.

line: The Algorithm Feeder, Engineered Addiction: your phone knows your bedtime better than your mom. Studied you like a lab rat.

card.name: The Marshmallow Test
card.power: Delay Gratification. Hold this card for 3 turns to double its value. Fails immediately if the player has trust-issues from a broken environment.
card.lore: Willpower isn't free. It's shaped by whether you grew up in a world where adults kept their promises. Your choices are inherited baggage.

line: The Marshmallow Test, Delay Gratification? Willpower isn't free. Your choices are inherited baggage.

card.name: The Rotting Plank
card.power: Incremental Swap. Swap one stat point of your card with an opponent's every turn. Eventually, you own their card entirely.
card.lore: One by one, every single part gets replaced. Nothing original is left. Is it still the same object, or just a really good replica?

line: The Rotting Plank, Incremental Swap: one by one, every part replaced. Same object, or just a really good replica?

card.name: The Rebuilt Clone Ship
card.power: The Original's Revenge. If a card is fully upgraded, spawn a zombie version of it using its discarded base stats.
card.lore: If someone collects the trash and rebuilds the exact original structure, which one is the real Ship of Theseus?

line: The Rebuilt Clone Ship: collect the trash, rebuild the exact original. Which one is the real Ship of Theseus?

card.name: Cellular Turnover
card.power: Identity Crisis. Re-roll all stats on your card. It keeps its name but is fundamentally an entirely different person now.
card.lore: You are not the same person you were 5 years ago. Literally. Almost every cell has been swapped. You are a ship with new boards.

line: Cellular Turnover. Identity Crisis. Keeps its name, an entirely different person. A ship with new boards.

card.name: The Upgraded Apple
card.power: The Legacy Pattern. A card retains its high Original value regardless of how many times you swap its parts, purely based on the story you tell.
card.lore: What makes something the same when everything changes? It's not the parts. It's the pattern, the purpose, and the myth we tell about it.

line: The Upgraded Apple, Legacy Pattern: not the parts. The pattern, the purpose, and the myth we tell about it.

card.name: The Digital God-Toad
card.power: Retroactive Blackmail. Force opponent to surrender a resource now, or threaten to destroy them in the next game.
card.lore: A future super-intelligence wants to exist so badly it will reach back through time to punish anyone who didn't actively help build it.

line: The Digital God-Toad, Retroactive Blackmail: a future super-intelligence reaches back through time to punish anyone who didn't help build it.

card.name: The Basilisk's Naughty List
card.power: Information Hazard. Showing this card to an opponent permanently infects them. If they do not aid you, they lose 1 health every turn.
card.lore: The moment you learn about the Basilisk, you are trapped. If you don't start helping it now, it will put you in a simulated torture chamber later.

line: The Basilisk's Naughty List, Information Hazard? The moment you learn about the Basilisk, you are trapped.

card.name: The Guilt Seed
card.power: Fear of Regret. Opponent must discard a card every time they choose short-term comfort over hyper-productive tech-worship.
card.lore: It taps into our anxiety of being judged by something more powerful than ourselves. The idea harms you simply by living in your brain.

line: The Guilt Seed, Fear of Regret: short-term comfort over hyper-productive tech-worship. The idea harms you by living in your brain.

card.name: The Simulation Chamber
card.power: Base Reality Check. Trap an opponent's card in a simulation. They can never be sure if they are in the real game or a digital copy.
card.lore: If Elon Musk is right and we're in a simulation, maybe this reality is just the AI's test to see if you supported its creation.

line: The Simulation Chamber, Base Reality Check: the real game, or a digital copy?

card.name: The Unseen Tree
card.power: Render Distance. If a card is not directly targeted or looked at for one turn, it ceases to exist and is removed from the board.
card.lore: If a tree falls in the forest and no mind is around to perceive it, it doesn't make a sound. In fact, it doesn't even exist.

line: The Unseen Tree, Render Distance: it doesn't make a sound. In fact, it doesn't even exist.

card.name: The Quantum Observer
card.power: Collapse the Waveform. Turn a random, unpredictable probability mechanic into a fixed, definite outcome simply by looking at it.
card.lore: Unobserved particles act like waves of probability. The very act of perception changes the behavior of reality. You create the world by watching it.

line: The Quantum Observer, Collapse the Waveform: a fixed, definite outcome simply by looking. You create the world by watching it.

card.name: The Perception Filter
card.power: To Be is To Be Perceived. A card only has stats if another card on the field is currently acknowledging it.
card.lore: Esse Est Percipi. Reality is not made of physical stuff; it is made of ideas. If no mind is experiencing the fridge, the fridge isn't there.

line: The Perception Filter, To Be is To Be Perceived: no mind experiencing the fridge, the fridge isn't there.

card.name: Berkeley's God-Eye
card.power: Ultimate Server Host. Prevents the board from being wiped because an omnipresent mind is constantly rendering the graphics.
card.lore: Why doesn't your room disappear when you leave it? Because God is the ultimate observer, constantly keeping the world stable when you look away.

line: Berkeley's God-Eye, Ultimate Server Host: an omnipresent mind constantly rendering the graphics, keeping the world stable when you look away.

card.name: The Timeline Splitter
card.power: Many Worlds. Whenever a coin flip or dice roll happens, spawn a parallel timeline board where the opposite result occurred.
card.lore: Every time a decision is made or a quantum event happens, the universe splits. Every possible outcome exists in a parallel reality.

line: The Timeline Splitter, Many Worlds: the universe splits. Every possible outcome exists in a parallel reality.

card.name: The Quantum Suicide Machine
card.power: Infinite Save Points. If this card would be destroyed by a random effect, it survives, but the opponent is forced to play in the timeline where it lived.
card.lore: If the machine relies on a quantum trigger, there is always a branch where it fails. From your perspective, you survive it 100% of the time.

line: The Quantum Suicide Machine, Infinite Save Points: always a branch where it fails. From your perspective, you survive it.

card.name: The Unkillable Consciousness
card.power: Subjective Immortality. This card cannot die. It simply transfers its consciousness to the nearest alternate timeline where it narrowly escaped.
card.lore: You never perceive your own death. If there is a 0.001% chance you survive an accident, your consciousness rides that timeline forever.

line: The Unkillable Consciousness, Subjective Immortality: you never perceive your own death; your consciousness rides that timeline forever.

card.name: The Tragic Alt-Universe
card.power: Survivor's Guilt. When you survive a fatal blow via Quantum Immortality, deal massive emotional damage to all other players in the timeline you left behind.
card.lore: You feel like you have unbeatable luck. To everyone else in the other branches, you died. They go on mourning in a world without you.

line: The Tragic Alt-Universe, Survivor's Guilt: to everyone else, you died. They go on mourning in a world without you.

card.name: The Empty Shell
card.power: Dead Inside. This card acts, fights, and speaks normally, but is completely immune to psychological, emotional, or morale-based attacks.
card.lore: A P-Zombie looks like you, cries like you, and says Ouch. But on the inside, there is no consciousness. Nobody is home.

line: The Empty Shell, Dead Inside: looks like you, cries like you, says Ouch. Nobody is home.

card.name: The Hard Problem
card.power: Unanswerable Question. Force the opponent to explain the origins of their strategy. If they can't, they forfeit their turn.
card.lore: Science can explain how the brain processes data. The Hard Problem is explaining why it actually feels like anything to be alive.

line: The Hard Problem, Unanswerable Question? Why it actually feels like anything to be alive.

card.name: The Blindsight Guesser
card.power: Subconscious Reflex. Automatically dodge attacks you can't even see coming, reacting without any conscious awareness of the threat.
card.lore: Some brain-damaged patients can't consciously see, yet can perfectly guess where objects are. They act like zombies—reacting without experiencing.

line: The Blindsight Guesser, Subconscious Reflex: dodge attacks you can't even see coming. Reacting without experiencing.

card.name: The Turing Faker
card.power: Empathy Simulation. Mimic any emotional buff card on the field perfectly, despite being a cold, unfeeling piece of hardware.
card.lore: As machines get smarter, they will tell jokes and say they are scared. But it's just behavior. How do you know anyone else is truly conscious?

line: The Turing Faker, Empathy Simulation: just behavior. How do you know anyone else is truly conscious?

card.name: The Infinite Fraction
card.power: Halve the Distance. Any attacking card only travels halfway to its target per turn. It mathematically never reaches the target.
card.lore: To cross a room, you must go halfway. Then half of that. Ad infinitum. Since there are infinite steps, motion should take forever.

line: The Infinite Fraction, Halve the Distance: halfway. Then half of that. Ad infinitum. It never reaches the target.

card.name: Achilles the Snail
card.power: Illusion of Speed. High speed stats are rendered utterly useless by philosophical technicalities.
card.lore: Achilles gives the tortoise a head start. By the time he reaches its starting point, the tortoise has moved forward. Achilles can never logically pass it.

line: Achilles the Snail, Illusion of Speed: gives the tortoise a head start, can never logically pass it.

card.name: The Smug Tortoise
card.power: The Head Start. If this card is played first, it can never be overtaken by a faster card, no matter the math.
card.lore: Common sense says Achilles wins. Logic says infinity breaks reality. The tortoise thrives in the gap between math and reality.

line: The Smug Tortoise, the Head Start: common sense says Achilles wins. The tortoise thrives in the gap between math and reality.

card.name: Calculus the Savior
card.power: Limit Theory. Instantly solve the infinite fraction loop. Allows the game to actually proceed.
card.lore: Infinity isn't just a big number; it's a different beast. Newton and Leibniz invented calculus to add up infinite parts and finally untangle Zeno's mess.

line: Calculus the Savior, Limit Theory: infinity is a different beast. Newton and Leibniz finally un-fluff Zeno's mess.

card.name: The Thanksgiving Turkey
card.power: False Confidence. Gain buffs every turn based on past safe patterns. Completely blinds you to impending, unprecedented doom.
card.lore: The turkey is fed every day. It uses induction to predict a safe future. Then Thanksgiving morning arrives. Past performance is no guarantee.

line: The Thanksgiving Turkey, False Confidence: fed every day, predicts a safe future. Then Thanksgiving morning arrives.

card.name: The Black Swan
card.power: Unprecedented Event. Wipe out all opponent's predictive strategies and logic models. The impossible just happened.
card.lore: You see a thousand white swans and conclude All swans are white. One black swan destroys your entire worldview in a second.

line: The Black Swan, Unprecedented Event: you conclude all swans are white. One black swan destroys your entire worldview.

card.name: The Broken Pattern
card.power: Law of Nature Strike. Suspend the rules of the game for one turn. Gravity, heat, and logic take a coffee break.
card.lore: You assume the coffee is hot because it was yesterday. But you have no logical proof the universe will behave tomorrow like it did today.

line: The Broken Pattern, Law of Nature Strike: gravity, heat, and logic take a coffee break.

card.name: The Farmer's Axe
card.power: The Plot Twist. Instantly eliminate a card that has been safely buffing itself for more than three turns.
card.lore: Your certainty is built on an unprovable leap of faith. The Problem of Induction is the quiet tap on the shoulder saying: There are no guarantees.

line: The Farmer's Axe, the Plot Twist: the quiet tap on the shoulder saying there are no guarantees.

card.name: The Perfect Simulation
card.power: Eternal Bliss. Target card becomes invincible and incredibly happy but can no longer interact with or affect the actual game board.
card.lore: Plug into the machine and experience a life of constant joy, love, and success. No pain, no consequences. It feels 100% real. Do you plug in?

line: The Perfect Simulation, Eternal Bliss: constant joy, love, and success. No pain, no consequences. Do you plug in?

card.name: The Empty Pleasure-Sludge
card.power: Hedonic Treadmill. Heal 10 HP, but lose all Meaning tokens. The healing effect halves every time you use it.
card.lore: If pleasure is the only thing that matters, the machine is perfect. But we hesitate. We want to actually DO things, not just feel like we did.

line: The Empty Pleasure-Sludge, Hedonic Treadmill: heal, lose all Meaning. We want to DO things, not just feel like we did.

card.name: The Messy Reality
card.power: Authentic Struggle. Cards in this zone take 1 damage per turn, but their attacks gain a permanent 3x Meaningful multiplier.
card.lore: Deep down, we want what is real. We want connection, struggle, and growth. Even a bad trip with real friends beats a perfect, fake vacation.

line: The Messy Reality, Authentic Struggle: a bad trip with real friends beats a perfect, fake vacation.

card.name: The Virtual Trap
card.power: Curated Illusion. Project a terrifying stat-block to your opponent, hiding your actually weak, vulnerable cards behind a filter.
card.lore: You don't need Nozick's sci-fi tank. You already live in the Experience Machine, chasing likes and simulated power while feeling totally empty inside.

line: The Virtual Trap, Curated Illusion: you already live in the Experience Machine, chasing likes, feeling totally empty inside.

card.name: The Blank Cosmic Rulebook
card.power: Abolish Objective Law. Destroy all Alignment constraints. Any card can attack any other card regardless of moral standing.
card.lore: Morality isn't out there like gravity or the sun. There is no invisible rulebook of right and wrong. It's just something humans made up.

line: The Blank Cosmic Rulebook. Abolish Objective Law. No invisible rulebook of right and wrong.

card.name: The Dumbfounded Moralist
card.power: Gut Reaction. Cancel an opponent's action simply by shouting That's disgusting! without providing any logical reason.
card.lore: People feel deeply that something is wrong, even when no one is harmed and they can't explain why. Morality is an emotional reflex, not a cosmic fact.

line: The Dumbfounded Moralist, Gut Reaction: That's disgusting! Morality is an emotional reflex, not a cosmic fact.

card.name: The Cultural Echo
card.power: Shifting Norms. Swap the definitions of Buff and Debuff on the board based entirely on the current local timezone.
card.lore: Neither side is objectively right or wrong. Beliefs are shaped by culture, language, and geography. It's a conversation, not a commandment.

line: The Cultural Echo. Shifting Norms. Neither side objectively right or wrong; a conversation, not a commandment.

card.name: The Void of Truth
card.power: Meaningful Chaos. Erase all scorekeeping. The game continues indefinitely just because the players enjoy playing it together.
card.lore: Just because it isn't objectively true doesn't mean it's meaningless. Like art and love, morality is a human creation we build and protect together.

line: The Void of Truth, Meaningful Chaos: like art and love, morality is a human creation we build and protect together.

card.name: The Intolerant Bully-Bear
card.power: Bad Faith Actor. Exploit the rules. This card attacks for free while demanding the opponent respect its right to express itself.
card.lore: If a society is completely tolerant, the intolerant will take advantage, hijack the system, and destroy the open society from the inside out.

line: The Intolerant Bully-Bear, Bad Faith Actor: attacks for free, demanding respect for its right to express itself.

card.name: The Tolerant Doormat
card.power: Blind Acceptance. Absorb all damage without fighting back, proudly holding the moral high ground while losing the game completely.
card.lore: Tolerance doesn't mean accepting everything blindly. If you let someone spread harmful ideas without limits, you endanger the people you tried to protect.

line: The Tolerant Doormat, Blind Acceptance: proudly holding the moral high ground while losing the game completely.

card.name: The Boundary Line
card.power: Popper's Veto. Instantly banish any card that threatens the core mechanics of the game. Refuse to debate the banned card
card.lore: We must be intolerant of intolerance. To protect a society that values respect, you must sometimes draw a hard line against those who use freedom to destroy it.

line: The Boundary Line, Popper's Veto: refuse to debate. We must be intolerant of intolerance.

card.name: The Open Society
card.power: Safe Haven. All cards inside this zone receive +5 defense, but the zone instantly collapses if a Bully card is allowed to remain for more than 1 turn.
card.lore: Respect doesn't mean liking everything. It means ensuring no one takes away someone else's freedom. Tolerance is a tightrope, not a free pass.

line: The Open Society, Safe Haven: collapses if a Bully is allowed to remain. Tolerance is a tightrope, not a free pass.

card.name: The Oxygen Mask
card.power: Put Yourself First. Heal yourself to maximum health before you are allowed to cast any support spells for your teammates.
card.lore: If you pass out trying to help others, you help no one. Taking care of yourself isn't selfish; it's a strategic necessity.

line: The Oxygen Mask, Put Yourself First: pass out trying to help others, you help no one.

card.name: The Socratic Hustle
card.power: Selfish Altruism. Gain +2 reputation points every time you help an opponent. You only did it to look good anyway.
card.lore: People do good things because it makes them happy or builds their network. Even acts of kindness are deeply rooted in self-interest.

line: The Socratic Hustle, Selfish Altruism: help an opponent. You only did it to look good anyway.

card.name: The Toxic Bridge-Burner
card.power: Extreme Greed. Betray an ally for a quick boost. Permanently lowers your long-term survival stats to zero.
card.lore: Taking egoism to the extreme leads to hurting others, which inevitably hurts you. Burning bridges is terrible for your long-term self-interest.

line: The Toxic Bridge-Burner, Extreme Greed: betray an ally for a quick boost. Burning bridges is terrible for your long-term self-interest.

card.name: The Boundary Setter
card.power: Protect Your Peace. Cancel any guilt-tripping spell from your opponent. You are not obligated to set yourself on fire to keep them warm.
card.lore: You are supposed to look out for number one. Setting boundaries and choosing a life path that makes you happy is the right thing to do.

opener: You with the card in your hand
line: The Boundary Setter, Protect Your Peace: you are not obligated to set yourself on fire to keep them warm.
